issues.description: Identifier naming inconsistency for the animal feeding method: the UML in the problem statement declares an abstract method named messageOnFeed() (problem_statement.md: line 28) and the solution implementation declares Animal.messageOnFeed() (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java: line 18) and implements it in subclasses (e.g., Seal.messageOnFeed() at solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Seal.java: line 13). However, other places in the problem text refer to the same concept as getFeedingSound() (problem_statement.md: lines 97 and 109-111). This mismatch (messageOnFeed vs getFeedingSound) can confuse students about which method to implement and which method Farm.feedAllAnimals() / Farm.singFarmSong() will call.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across all artifacts. Preferred action: update the problem statement to consistently use messageOnFeed() (as shown in the UML and the solution) and replace all occurrences of getFeedingSound() with messageOnFeed() (including the feedAllAnimals()/singFarmSong descriptions). If instead getFeedingSound() is the desired API, rename the abstract method and all implementations in the template/solution to getFeedingSound(). Ensure example calls in the description (e.g., feedAllAnimals and singFarmSong) reference the same method name.
